title: Support for late-peaking athletes under Singapore's spex sports funding programmes
asked: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked how spexPotential accounts for sports where athletes peak later, how long athletes can be supported before senior representation, and how the Ministry avoids disadvantaging them through early progression benchmarks.
response: Mr David Neo said support is designed around an athlete's current performance and assessed potential rather than age alone, and that no limit is placed on how long athletes can be supported if they meet the criteria. The spex framework — spexScholarship, spexPotential and spexCarding — calibrates support across an athlete's career, including late bloomers and those who switch sports. He cited Paralympian Theresa Goh, supported by spexCarding at 14, spexScholarship at 27 and spexCarding again at 38 as a shooter. On the supplementary, he said the athlete in question was supported by spexCarding and spexGLOW, and that the Ministry is open to looking at wider windows and different data points.

key_points.point: Support is based on current performance and assessed potential, not solely age, and there is no cap on how long an athlete can be supported if criteria are met.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: we do not place a limit on how long athletes can be supported as long as they meet performance and potential criteria

key_points.point: spexPotential gives targeted financial and programmatic support to athletes with the potential to win SEA Games gold, bridging them towards the spexScholarship.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: The spexPotential programme, in particular, provides targeted financial and programmatic support to athletes with the potential to achieve gold medal success at the Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games).

key_points.point: spexPotential applies to athletes of all ages and is based on the developmental stage of the sport's high performance pathway.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: The spexPotential programme also supports athletes based on their developmental stage of their sport’s high performance pathway and it applies to athletes of all ages.

key_points.point: The framework covers late bloomers and athletes who switch sports.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: The spex framework also supports late bloomers or athletes who switch sports.

key_points.point: Paralympian Theresa Goh was supported by spexCarding from age 14 and received the spexScholarship at 27.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: As a swimmer, she was supported by spexCarding from when she was 14 years old and was awarded the spexScholarship when she was 27 years old.

key_points.point: The SEA Games sprinter raised in the supplementary question was supported by spexCarding and spexGLOW, which allowed full-time training for a specific period.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: he was supported by our spexCarding programme, and the spexGLOW programme, which allowed him to train full-time for a specific period of time

key_points.point: The Ministry is open to looking at wider windows and different data points in how athletes are supported.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: we are definitely open to looking at the wider windows, different data points

left_open: Whether the window for considering spex grants will be formally extended for older athletes
How older athletes' work, family and other responsibilities are factored into support decisions
supplementary: Whether the spex grant consideration window could be widened for older athletes, and support for a SEA Games gold medallist not on the spex programme.
